watermark_verification.reason: Provider watermark verification was not requested.

normalisation.note: Unicode normalisation differences can be legitimate typography. They are reported as forensic observations, not provenance proof.

unicode_forensics.note: Observable Unicode artefacts can reveal hidden or unusual text channels, but they are not equivalent to provider watermarks.

signals.name: type_token_ratio
signals.interpretation: Vocabulary diversity metric only; not an AI or watermark test.

signals.name: sentence_length_cv
signals.interpretation: Variation in sentence length; both human and AI writing span the full range.

signals.name: repeated_trigram_types
signals.interpretation: Counts repeated three-word sequences; repetition alone does not identify authorship.

stylometry.note: Stylometry describes writing patterns. It is not a provider watermark detector and cannot prove AI authorship.

c2pa.reason: C2PA inspection applies to supported files, not raw pasted text.
c2pa.note: C2PA can provide signed, tamper-evident provenance for supported assets. A valid manifest is evidence about an asset history, not proof that every word was originally authored by a named model.

evidence_summary.interpretation: No positive provenance evidence was established by the configured checks. Absence of evidence is not evidence of human authorship.
evidence_summary.note: This is an evidence-strength classification, not a probability that text was AI-generated.

evidence_scores.note: Scores describe strength within separate evidence channels. They must not be added together or interpreted as an AI-authorship probability.

limitations: A provider watermark is not the same as generic AI-style detection.
Short samples usually provide less signal than long passages.
Absence of a detectable mark does not prove human authorship or absence of AI processing.
Unicode and stylometric findings are observational and can have ordinary non-AI explanations.
C2PA proves statements bound to an asset when validation succeeds; it does not by itself prove that every word was originally generated by the named software.
